To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have introduced a numerical method for the computation of periodic solutions of the vortex-sheet problem with surface tension, and we have computed a family of smooth breathers for the case of equal densities on both sides of the interface.

the vortex sheet with symmetric surface tension can support breathers that are smooth and symmetric, and that the bifurcations that occur in the bifurcation diagrams of these breathers are of the fold, pitchfork, and Hopf types, and can occur at the same value of the surface tension parameter.

we have developed a numerical method to compute time-periodic solutions for the vortex sheet with capillary forces, and that we have computed a family of symmetric, time-dependent vortex sheets with surface-tension separating two immiscibly fluids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics of the vortex sheet.
the study of the evolution of a vortex sheet separating two immiscibile fluids of equal density, in which the interface tension plays an important role.
the numerical solution of the Euler equations in two space dimensions, for a flow of an inviscid fluid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vortex sheet with a flat interface is unstable with respect to symmetric perturbations of the interface.

the problem of computing periodic solutions to the Euler equations with a surface tension boundary condition, and the related variational formulation, is not as well behaved as the corresponding problem for vortex sheets without a surface tension boundary.
the bifurcations are all of saddle-node type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method for computing periodic solutions of the vortex-sheet equation and have found a family of solutions for which the interface is smooth and periodic.
the bifurcated branches of the bifurcation diagrams are not connected to the trivial solution.
we have shown that the bifurcated solutions are not stable and that they are not connected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a numerical technique based on a variational formulation can be used to efficiently find time-periodic solutions in the context of a free-boundary problem.
the presence of surface tension is essential in the bifurcation of symmetric solutions of the vortex-sheet problem.
the bifurcating branch of symmetric, time-dependent solutions is very complicated and that, in general, the bifurcations of the rest states do not lead to periodic solutions.
